label: token right after an early g (g at position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the step right after the letter g is input, but only when that g was original token 0 or 1 (so the feature is active at t=1 or t=2). Precision is 1.0 on dev: every such step is active. It is strongest when g is the first token (t=1, about 0.95-1.0 of max), a bit weaker when g is second (t=2, about 0.8-0.9). The token being input at the active step barely matters. It does not fire after a g at position 2 or later (only traces at t=3), and it does not fire in the delimiter or copy phases. The steps it misses (about 14% of active steps but only 0.3% of activation mass) are near-zero activations at t=1 after other first tokens such as 2, y or j.

issues: Minor: the 'misses' are effectively zero activations (shown as 0.00 relative) at t=1 after first tokens such as 2 and y. They make up 14% of active steps but only 0.3% of mass, so they are threshold-level noise, not a separate behavior.

Minor: there are a few traces outside the predicate. At t=3 after g, 6% of steps are active and they hold 0.24% of mass. There are also 63 copy-phase steps on test (49 on dev, all at t=5 / recall_idx 2), with about 0.02% of mass. 'Does not fire in the copy phase' is very nearly true but not strictly true.
